facts.statement: The genus Aoniraptor contains only one known species, Aoniraptor libertatem, which is known from a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Aoniraptor libertatem, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in 2010 but was not formally described until 2016.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 2010, but only formally described in 2016.

facts.statement: The species name "libertatem" refers to freedom and commemorates the bicentennial of Argentina's independence from Spain in 1810.
facts.quote: The specific name, libertatem, comes from the Latin word for freedom, as it was discovered on the bicentennial of Argentina's independence from Spain in 1810.

facts.statement: Aoniraptor grew to a length of up to 6 meters.
facts.quote: Aoniraptor grew up to 6 m long.

facts.statement: In 2016, researchers identified three unique distinctive traits, or autapomorphies, in Aoniraptor.
facts.quote: En 2016, se identificaron tres rasgos únicos distintivos, o autapomorfias.

facts.statement: The front-central tail vertebrae have anterior joint projections without clear articulation surfaces to contact the fan-shaped posterior joint projections.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola media frontal tiene proyecciones conjuntas anteriores que son, sin superficies de la articulación claras con el fin de hacer contacto con los salientes de las articulaciones traseras en forma de abanico.

facts.statement: The front-central tail vertebrae possess anterior articular projections with a thick, blunt projection on the exterior.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola media frontal tiene protuberancias articulares anteriores con un saliente grueso y romo en el exterior.

facts.statement: The central-rear tail vertebrae have paired flattening areas that are not articulation surfaces, located at the upper rear corners of their vertebral bodies.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola posterior central ha emparejado aplanamientos, al no ser superficies de la articulación, a las esquinas superiores traseras de sus cuerpos vertebrales.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses classify Aoniraptor as a member of the Megaraptora group.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses including Aoniraptor recover it as a megaraptoran.

facts.statement: Aoniraptor is classified within the superfamily Tyrannosauroidea and the clade Megaraptora, but outside the family Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: Aoniraptor fue incluido dentro de la superfamilia Tyrannosauroidea y dentro de esta, en el clado Megaraptora, pero por fuera de la familia Megaraptoridae.

facts.statement: While the description supports the view that these theropods were tyrannosauroids, other researchers consider them to be part of the Carnosauria group.
facts.quote: El artículo de descripción apoya la interpretación de Novas et al. de que estos terópodos eran parte de los tiranosauroideos; sin embargo, otros investigadores consideran que eran parte de otro grupo de tetanuranos, los Carnosauria.

facts.statement: It has been informally suggested that Aoniraptor might be a synonym of the theropod Gualicho due to similarities in their tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Por otra parte, se ha sugerido informalmente que Aoniraptor podría ser un sinónimo de otro terópodo, Gualicho, también descubierto en el área de Huincul, debido a las similitudes de sus vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: Aoniraptor lived between the middle and late Cretaceous, approximately 97 to 95 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió entre mediados a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 97 a 95 millones de años, entre el Cenomaniense medio y el Turoniense temprano, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range for Aoniraptor as the Albian stage, from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)
